portName: Port of Piraeus cruise terminals (Miaoulis, Themistocles, Alkimos)
seoTitle: Athens cruise port (Piraeus): metro to the Acropolis
seoDescription: Piraeus cruise port 2026: terminals A, B and C, metro Line 1 or 3 to Monastiraki for €1.20, X80 bus on a €4.10 day ticket, Acropolis €30 with timed entry.
quickAnswer: Ships dock at Piraeus, about 10 km from the Acropolis, at Terminal A (Miaoulis, Gate E11) or Terminals B and C (Themistocles and Alkimos, Gate E12). Walk 15–30 minutes to the metro and take Line 1 or Line 3 to Monastiraki, about 20 minutes, on a €1.20 ticket (2026). Be on a train back from central Athens at least 2 hours 45 minutes before all-aboard.
intro: Piraeus is a working port city, not Athens itself. The Acropolis is about 10 km away, so every plan starts with the metro, the seasonal X80 bus or a taxi. The metro is cheap and frequent, but the walk from the gates to the stations is longer than most people expect, especially from Terminals B and C. The other fixed point is the Acropolis ticket: entry is by timed slot, and summer morning slots sell out. Book it before you sail and build the day around it.

terminals.name: Terminal A "Miaoulis" (Gate E11, Akti Miaouli)
terminals.notes: Closest terminal to the town side of the port. About 15 minutes on foot to Dimotiko Theatro metro (Line 3). The port authority runs a free shuttle between the ships and the passenger terminals.

terminals.name: Terminal B "Themistocles" (Gate E12)
terminals.notes: Further along the cruise quays at Akti Miaouli and Akti Xaveriou. About 30 minutes on foot to the metro. Opened in its extended form in 2013.

terminals.name: Terminal C "Alkimos" (Gate E12)
terminals.notes: Shares Gate E12 with Terminal B. About 30 minutes on foot to the metro. Terminal assignments can change at short notice; check your daily programme.

walkability.detail: Athens is not walkable from the ship. The realistic walk is to the metro: about 15 minutes from Terminal A to Dimotiko Theatro (Line 3), and about 30 minutes from Terminals B and C to Dimotiko Theatro or Piraeus station (Lines 1 and 3). The route is flat along the busy port road. In the city, Monastiraki to the Acropolis entrance is 10–15 minutes uphill on foot.

transportSections.time: About 20 min to Monastiraki, about 23 min to Syntagma
transportSections.detail: Line 3 was extended to Piraeus in October 2022, with Dimotiko Theatro as the terminus; it is the nearest station to Terminal A. Buy tickets at the machines or tap a contactless bank card at the gate for a 90-minute fare. Change at Syntagma to Line 2 for Akropoli station, one stop on, close to the Acropolis Museum and the south slope entrance.

transportSections.time: About 17 min to Monastiraki; about 15 min to Thissio
transportSections.detail: Line 1 starts at Piraeus station, next to the ferry harbour and a 30-minute walk from Terminals B and C. Thissio and Monastiraki are both a short uphill walk to the Acropolis. Line 1 is older and the more crowded line; keep bags closed.

transportSections.cost: No single ticket: €4.10 24-hour ticket or €20 3-day tourist ticket (2026)
transportSections.detail: Seasonal cruise-day line, relaunched on 23 May 2026. It runs from the cruise terminals to the Acropolis stop on Dionysiou Areopagitou and to Syntagma. The standard €1.20 90-minute ticket is not valid on the X80. Ask at the terminal information desk whether it is still running on your date.

transportSections.cost: Metered; insist the meter is running
transportSections.detail: Yellow taxis wait at the terminals. Ride-hailing apps such as Uber and Free Now supply licensed taxis. Traffic between Piraeus and the centre is heavy at peak times, so the metro is usually more predictable on the way back.
The Piraeus Port Authority runs a free shuttle between the ships and the passenger terminals. It does not go to the metro; the walk to the station starts at the terminal building.

returnTiming.rule: Be on a metro train from Monastiraki or Syntagma by 14:45 for a 17:30 all-aboard if docked at Terminal A, or by 14:30 at Terminals B or C.
returnTiming.detail: The train takes about 20 minutes, then it is 15 minutes on foot to Terminal A or 30 minutes to Terminals B and C, plus the shuttle to the ship. That puts you on board around 16:00, 90 minutes before all-aboard, with a margin for a slow train, a crowded platform or a wrong exit. Strikes in Greece are regular and sometimes called at short notice.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If the metro is stopped, take a taxi from central Athens and tell the driver the terminal and gate (E11 or E12). Call the port agent number printed in your daily programme as soon as you know you will be late.

diyVsExcursion.item: Typical DIY day: day ticket, Acropolis and Acropolis Museum
diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner

excursionAdvice: A DIY Athens day is straightforward for anyone comfortable with a metro and a 30-minute walk. The ship's tour earns its price if you could not get an Acropolis slot, if a transport strike is announced for your call, in peak heat, or for anyone with limited mobility, because coach drop-offs cut most of the walking. For the Corinth Canal or Cape Sounion, a ship tour is the safer way to fit the drive into one call.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at 08:00 at Terminal A and an Acropolis ticket booked for the 10:00 slot. Add 15 minutes each way from Terminals B and C.

steps.what: Leave the ship, take the free shuttle to the terminal if needed, and walk about 15 minutes to Dimotiko Theatro station.
Buy a €4.10 24-hour ticket or tap a contactless card, and take Line 3 to Monastiraki (about 20 minutes).
Walk up through Plaka towards the Acropolis entrance, 10–15 minutes uphill. Coffee on the way.
Enter the Acropolis in your timed slot. Allow about 2 hours for the Propylaia, Parthenon, Erechtheion and the views.
Walk down to the Acropolis Museum (€20) for about 75 minutes, including the Parthenon Gallery.
Lunch around Monastiraki: souvlaki or gyros on or near Monastiraki Square.
Take Line 3 from Monastiraki back to Dimotiko Theatro.
Walk back to Terminal A (about 15 minutes) and go through security.

sights.name: Acropolis and the Parthenon
sights.why: The reason most passengers come: the Parthenon, Erechtheion and Propylaia above the city.
sights.cost: €30 all year, €15 reduced (2026; the winter half-price ticket has ended); free for EU citizens up to 25 and non-EU visitors under 18
sights.tip: Entry is by timed slot. Book through the official Hellenic Heritage ticket site (tickets.hh.gr / hhticket.gr) before the cruise; tickets are non-refundable. On free days you still need to reserve a slot. The old combined multi-site ticket is no longer sold. Winter hours from 1 November: 08:00–17:00, last admission 16:40 (Athens Tourism, 23 October 2026). Bring water and a hat: on extreme heat days the site has closed from 12:00 to 17:00.

sights.name: Acropolis Museum
sights.why: The original sculptures from the Acropolis, with a glass-floored view of an excavated neighbourhood below.
sights.tip: Summer hours (to 31 October) are 09:00–20:00 Tuesday to Sunday, to 22:00 on Fridays, but only 09:00–17:00 on Mondays. Two minutes from Akropoli metro.

sights.name: Ancient Agora
sights.why: The civic centre of ancient Athens, with the Temple of Hephaestus, one of the best-preserved Greek temples.
sights.tip: Close to Thissio and Monastiraki stations, so easy to fit between the Acropolis and the train back.

sights.name: Plaka and Anafiotika
sights.why: The old neighbourhood under the north slope of the Acropolis, with stepped lanes and small whitewashed houses in Anafiotika.
sights.tip: Restaurants on the main Plaka streets charge for the location; walk a street or two back to eat.

sights.name: National Archaeological Museum
sights.why: Greece's largest collection of ancient art, including the Mask of Agamemnon and the Antikythera Mechanism.
sights.tip: Summer hours (to 15 November 2026) are 08:00–20:00, but on Tuesdays it opens only at 13:00. Victoria station on Line 1 is the nearest stop.

sights.name: Panathenaic Stadium
sights.why: The marble stadium of the first modern Olympic Games in 1896.
sights.tip: Open 08:00–19:00 from March to October and 08:00–17:00 from November to February. Tickets are valid on the day of issue only.

sights.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
sights.why: The remaining columns of what was the largest temple in Greece, next to Hadrian's Arch.
sights.tip: Much of it can be seen from the railings outside; pay only if you want to walk among the columns.

sights.name: Roman Agora and Tower of the Winds
sights.why: A compact Roman market site with an octagonal marble clock tower, on the edge of Plaka.
sights.tip: A short stop on the walk between the Acropolis and Monastiraki.

beaches.name: Votsalakia beach, Piraeus
beaches.howToGetThere: At the foot of Kastella hill, just beyond the Mikrolimano harbour on Leoforos Vasileos Pavlou; a short taxi ride from the cruise terminals.
beaches.note: The nearest town beach to the cruise port, with free and organised sections. Mikrolimano next to it is a good place for a fish lunch. Athens is not a beach port; the Riviera beaches further south need more time.

food.dish: Pork souvlaki in pita with tomato sauce
food.where: Kostas, Plateia Agias Irinis 2, Monastiraki (weekdays only, cash, sells out by mid-afternoon)

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at the Acropolis without a timed ticket.
commonMistakes.fix: Book a slot on the official Hellenic Heritage site before the cruise. Summer morning slots sell out.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming the walk to the metro is short.
commonMistakes.fix: Allow 15 minutes from Terminal A and 30 minutes from Terminals B and C, each way. Check your terminal in the daily programme.

commonMistakes.mistake: Boarding the X80 with a €1.20 ticket.
commonMistakes.fix: The X80 accepts only the €4.10 24-hour ticket or the €20 3-day tourist ticket. Buy the day ticket before you board.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning the Acropolis Museum for a Monday afternoon.
commonMistakes.fix: On Mondays it closes at 17:00 and last entry is 16:30. Visit it straight after the Acropolis.

commonMistakes.mistake: Visiting the National Archaeological Museum on a Tuesday morning.
commonMistakes.fix: It opens at 13:00 on Tuesdays. Swap the order of the day.
Strikes on the metro and buses are regular and sometimes announced at short notice. Check the evening before and the morning you dock, and keep the ship's tour as a fallback.

safety: Athens is safe for daytime visitors, but theft of wallets, phones and passports is common on the metro and in crowded tourist areas. Line 1 and the stations at Monastiraki, Omonia and Syntagma are the usual hotspots, as are the Monastiraki flea market and the approach to the Acropolis. Keep bags closed and in front, and phones in pockets. Demonstrations often gather on Syntagma Square; stay away from them. In summer, heat is a real risk on the exposed Acropolis rock: carry water and a hat. Greece sends emergency alerts to phones for heat and wildfires.
scams: The friendly stranger who suggests a bar near Monastiraki or Syntagma, then leaves before an inflated bill arrives. Decline invitations from people you have just met.
Taxi drivers who do not start the meter, or say it is broken, and then name a fare. Check the meter is running before you set off, or book through a ride-hailing app.
The 'free' bracelet or flower pressed into your hand, followed by a demand for money. Hand it back and walk on.
Unofficial Acropolis 'skip-the-line' tickets sold on the street. Buy only from the official Hellenic Heritage ticket site.
accessibility: The walk from the terminals to the metro is long, especially from Terminals B and C, so step-free access into Athens is easiest by taxi or a ship's accessible tour. The Acropolis has a lift on the north face for visitors with disabilities and limited mobility. In summer 2026 it stopped repeatedly for wind over Beaufort 5, heavy rain, prolonged high temperatures and maintenance, so it cannot be relied on; the paths on top are uneven and slippery marble. The Acropolis Museum is the most accessible of the main sights. For limited mobility, a ship's accessible tour is the safer choice.
rainyDay: The Acropolis Museum and the National Archaeological Museum are the best wet-day plans; together they fill most of a call. The Acropolis rock is slippery marble in rain, and the lift for visitors with limited mobility can stop in heavy rain.
crowdTips: Piraeus handled 863 cruise calls and about 1.85 million cruise passengers in 2025, and several ships often share a day. The Acropolis is busiest in the early slots, when ship tours arrive. A late-morning or early-afternoon slot can be quieter but is hotter in summer. Monastiraki and Plaka are packed from late morning. Morning trains towards the centre and afternoon trains back to Piraeus fill with cruise passengers; leave earlier rather than later.

faqs.q: Is Athens walkable from the Piraeus cruise port?
faqs.a: No. The Acropolis is about 10 km away. Walk 15–30 minutes to the metro and take Line 1 or Line 3 to Monastiraki, about 20 minutes.

faqs.q: How do I get from Piraeus cruise port to the Acropolis?
faqs.a: Walk to Dimotiko Theatro (Line 3) or Piraeus (Line 1), ride to Monastiraki, and walk 10–15 minutes uphill. Or take Line 3 to Syntagma and Line 2 one stop to Akropoli. A 90-minute ticket is €1.20; a 24-hour ticket is €4.10 (2026).
No. Ships dock at the cruise quays and use Terminal A (Miaoulis), B (Themistocles) or C (Alkimos). The port authority provides free transport for any passengers landed from ships at anchor.

faqs.q: Is the X80 bus still running?
faqs.a: OASA relaunched the X80 Piraeus–Akropoli–Syntagma express for the season on 23 May 2026. It needs a €4.10 day ticket or €20 3-day ticket. Ask at the terminal information desk whether it is running on your date.

faqs.q: Do I need to book the Acropolis in advance?
faqs.a: Yes. Entry is by timed slot and costs €30 (2026). Book on the official Hellenic Heritage site before the cruise; summer morning slots sell out.

faqs.q: Is there a cruise passenger fee in Greece?
faqs.a: Yes. Since 21 July 2025 each passenger who disembarks pays a fee per port call. For Piraeus it is €5 from June to September, €3 in April, May and October and €1 from November to March. Cruise lines collect it, often on the onboard account.

faqs.q: What can I do in Athens in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The Acropolis and the Acropolis Museum, lunch in Monastiraki and a walk through Plaka fit comfortably. Add the Ancient Agora if time allows. Be on a train back at least 2 hours 45 minutes before all-aboard.

faqs.q: Is Athens safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes in daytime, with care. Pickpockets work the metro, especially Line 1, and crowded areas around Monastiraki and the Acropolis. Avoid demonstrations on Syntagma Square.
